# Healthcare ETL — Data Quality Report

**Database:** `healthcare_etl` &nbsp;|&nbsp; **Pipeline:** `src/etl.py` &nbsp;|&nbsp; **Generated by:** `src/validation.py`

> This report is regenerated automatically on every full pipeline run
> (`python src/etl.py`) and saved to `docs/data_quality_report.md`. The
> figures below are from a representative run — exact counts vary slightly
> between runs because the source generator (`generate_data.py`) does not
> use a fixed random seed for row-level content.

---

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Total source rows read | 14,100 (1,100 patients + 5,500 appointments + 7,500 treatments) |
| Rows after cleaning | 11,481 (1,066 patients + 4,522 appointments + 5,893 treatments) |
| Schema/dtype mismatches found | 0 ✅ |

## 4. Post-Cleaning Row Counts

| Table | Rows before | Rows after cleaning | Rows dropped |
|---|---|---|---|
| Patients | 1,100 | 1,066 | 34 (duplicates) |
| Appointments | 5,500 | 4,522 | 978 (duplicates + orphans) |
| Treatments | 7,500 | 5,893 | 1,607 (duplicates + orphans) |

> **Note on the drop counts:** appointment orphans are checked against the
> already-deduplicated patient set, and treatment orphans are checked
> against the already-cleaned, orphan-free appointment set — cleaning is
> applied in dependency order so that dropping bad parent rows correctly
> cascades to newly-orphaned child rows.

## How to regenerate this report

```bash
python src/etl.py
```

This re-extracts the source CSVs, re-runs every check above, and rewrites
`docs/data_quality_report.md` with current figures — always reflecting the
most recent pipeline run, never manually edited.
